assumptions: Sorting result keys is preferred to insertion order because determinism across replicas matters more than the author's key order
The trial seeder writes observations with a strict body and no result.summary, so the key=value fallback is the common case
constraints: D51: ordering, class labels, budget accounting and truncation must stay identical; 2.x stores untouched
worktree isolation: no dist build, single vitest process, tsc last
context: D51/DP-0: working-set renderRecord now renders observation substance (source_kind [uri] via check_method · at observed_at · volatile · base..head, head = result.summary or sorted scalar key=value ≤240) and 'revision base..head' (8-hex) on every scope line; 10 tests added (red on old renderer); repo_id/repo_ids mismatch assessed, not fixed.
rationale: sorted keys keep payload_hash replay-stable across replicas, scalars-only keeps one line per fact, and the bound stops one verbose check from eating the 6000-char budget
summary: Chose to render an observation's result as sorted top-level scalar key=value pairs (bounded to 240 chars, whitespace collapsed, nested values skipped) when result.summary is absent, over JSON.stringify or insertion-order rendering
